pass_a_gloss: But (it is) likely, Ambrose most god-fearing and industrious and Tatiana most modest and manly (from whom to have departed womanly things — as they departed from Sarah — I pray already), that you are at a loss why, our treatise lying before us concerning prayer, these things in prefaces concerning impossibilities for men made possible by God's grace have been said. I am persuaded that to make clear the whole treatise concerning prayer exactly and worthily of God — both how one must pray and what to say to God in prayer and which times are fitter than which times for prayer — is, on account of our weakness, one of the impossibilities. [Thesis + program.] The one of these — the 'what' — is prayer's words; the 'how' the pray-er disposition. Examples of each kind (agraphon, John 3:12/Matt 6:33, Luke 6:28, Matt 9:38, Luke 22:40; Matt 24:20, Matt 6:7, 1 Tim 2:8-10, Matt 5:23-24, 1 Cor 7:5, Mark 11:25, 1 Cor 11:4-5) with Origen's fragrant-word and marriage-mysteries exposition. But Paul, knowing all these and far more from Law, prophets and Gospel fullness, and able to set them out — seeing how far we fall short of the 'what as we ought' — adds whence the lack is filled: the Spirit intercedes with unutterable groans (Rom 8:26-27); the Abba-Spirit takes up our groans (Rom 8:15); three tiers of conquerors (Rom 8:37). Attached: 1 Cor 14:14-15 (spirit and mind); the mind prays only if the Spirit first prays as accompaniment; the Spirit hymns first, having searched the depths (1 Cor 2:10). A disciple, sensing human weakness, asked 'Lord, teach us' (Luke 11:1, quoted whole); John too taught something more-than-prophetic, in secret (lacuna: Matt 3:5-6?); truly spiritual prayers were written down — Hannah's in part (1 Sam 1), Psalms titled prayer (LXX 16/89/101), full of doctrines (Hos 14:10). Since expounding prayer needs Father, firstborn Word and Spirit (Col 1:15/Heb 1:6), the author prays as a man for a full spiritual discourse before beginning.
